title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hook and metrics integration
author: Jordan Patel
description: Summary: Add a CI hook and metrics integration for per-prompt regression checks in the eval-harness. Motivation: We need automated, per-prompt regression detection in CI so that changes to runtime, tokenization, model variants, or prompt normalization do not silently degrade prompt-level quality. This PR introduces a GitHub Actions workflow, a small CI hook that uploads per-prompt metrics to our eval metrics service, and a quality gating step that can fail CI on regressions above configured thresholds. - What this includes (checklist): - [x] GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/eval-per-prompt-regression.yml - [x] CI hook implementation and uploader: eval-harness/ci/hooks/prompt_regression_hook.py - [x] Eval metrics client and minimal schema changes: eval-harness/metrics/client.py (backwards compatible) - [x] Example prompt-set and sample baseline: eval-harness/tests/prompt_sets/customer_support.yaml - [x] README updates describing how to add new prompt-sets and tune thresholds - [x] Unit tests for hook and uploader - Behavior and design notes: The workflow runs per-PR on changes under eval-harness/** and on a schedule for nightly baselines. It runs the existing prompt-set eval runner, computes per-prompt metrics (accuracy, BLEU-like similarity, hallucination flags), and compares to stored baselines in S3. If any prompt falls below a configurable delta (default: 5% absolute or 10% relative, configurable via .github/eval-config.yml or repo-level secrets), the job will post a detailed regression report artifact and mark the quality gate step as failed. The uploader posts aggregated metrics to the eval-metrics service (internal) so dashboards and alerts can be tied to PR-level runs. - Backward compatibility: Metrics client uses a feature flag (EVAL_METRICS_UPLOAD=true) toggled by repo secrets/ci config. If disabled, the hook falls back to storing artifacts only. The client is intentionally lightweight and paginates uploads to avoid CI timeouts. - Security considerations: The uploader uses short-lived CI credentials and does not include raw model outputs in uploads — only aggregated metrics and anonymized prompt IDs. Secrets required: EVAL_METRICS_API_KEY (scoped write-only), S3_BASELINE_BUCKET. - Related work: ENG-4276 (per-prompt regression gating), ENG-4321 (eval metrics service onboarding).
